errors.text_span: The chart contains six slices, each representing a different attribute.
errors.evidence: The figure is not a pie chart with six slices. It is a conceptual diagram showing a circle divided into four equal quadrants, each representing a category. The model has misinterpreted the outer labels as separate slices.
The yellow quadrant is labeled "Complexity" on the interior. "Uncrushable" is an associated external label, not the primary label of the quadrant itself.

errors.text_span: occupies approximately 15% of the total area.
errors.evidence: The yellow quadrant is one of four equal quadrants, meaning it occupies 25% of the circle, not 15%. Similar errors are made for other quadrants (e.g., 20% for red and green).

errors.text_span: Below that is an orange slice labeled “Auto-verifiable”, taking up approximately 15% of the space.
errors.evidence: There is no orange slice in the chart. The quadrant associated with the "Auto-verifiable" label is red, not orange, and there is no slice corresponding to this label alone.
The blue quadrant is labeled "Instance" on the interior. "Unhackable" is the associated external label.

errors.text_span: Finally, there is a smaller green slice labeled “General” which seems to account for around 5% of the chart.
errors.evidence: There is no smaller green slice. "General" is an external label for the main green quadrant, which occupies 25% of the circle.

errors.text_span: Each slice includes a small icon alongside its label.
errors.evidence: The icons are positioned next to the inner labels ("Complexity", "Instance", "Scalable Oversight", "Coverage"), not the outer labels that the description uses to identify the "slices" (e.g., "Uncrushable"). This creates an incorrect association.

The description completely omits the primary labels for two of the four quadrants: "Complexity" and "Instance". It also fails to describe the key structural feature of each quadrant having both an inner label with an icon and an outer label in a colored box.

errors.text_span: the slices appear to be arranged in a clockwise orientation based on size.
errors.evidence: The four quadrants are all equal in size (25% each). The claim that they are ordered by size is false and based on the previously hallucinated incorrect proportions.
